item.title: Can Bukele’s Show of Force Bring Peace to Haiti?
item.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele deployed an additional 2,000 troops to Haiti following the kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians. Whether Bukele’s approach can help restore stability in Haiti, and how the international community will respond, remains to be seen.

item.title: Data Vulnerabilities in U.S.-China Competition
item.description: The United States often solely discusses data through the lens of enabling innovation, while data in fact presents an asymmetric threat surface in competition, and potential conflict, with China.

item.title: Loopholes Are for Exporters, Not Just Taxpayers
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses new U.S. regulations to limit Chinese access to advanced AI chips and the challenges of enforcing them.

item.title: Evolution of Energy Markets in 2026: Supply Bottlenecks and the Search for Problem-Free Barrels
item.description: Despite a security corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, refined oil product prices remain high, and policy interventions have offered little relief. The conflict in Iran strengthens the case for local supply, diesel efficiency, and biofuels.

item.title: Winning the Space Race Will Require a Diplomatic Victory at WRC-27
item.description: As China lands a reusable rocket and plans massive low-Earth orbit satellite constellations, the United States cannot take its lead in this critical technology for granted. Securing U.S. satellite leadership requires effective diplomacy before and during the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference in Shanghai.

item.title: Rising U.S. Yields and Their Implications for Emerging Markets
item.description: Driven by real, inflation, and reaction-function shocks, the persistent rise in government bond yields since the February onset of conflict in the Middle East has mixed implications for emerging markets and developing economies.

item.title: Experts React: Takeaways from President Trump’s Trip to Asia
item.description: CSIS experts react to President Trump’s trip to China and share their reactions to the ASEAN Summit, Quad leaders’ meeting, APEC Summit, and Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral meeting.
